keywords: how should a bracelet fit on your wrist
how should a chain bracelet fit
how should a cuff bracelet fit
how should a men's bracelet fit
how are bracelets supposed to fit
answer: A bracelet fits when it rests just above your wrist bone, you can slide one or two fingers (about ½–1 in) underneath, and it moves a little without sliding down over your hand. For most chain bracelets that means a length about ½–1 in longer than your wrist measurement. Cuffs and bangles follow slightly different rules.
intro: How a bracelet should fit depends on its type. A chain can be adjusted for snug or loose; a bangle has to pass over your hand, so it's always a bit loose; a cuff sits open and should grip lightly. Start with your wrist measurement and add room according to the style and how you like to wear it.

checklist.good: One finger slides under a snug bracelet, or two under a looser chain, without stretching it.
checklist.tooTight: No finger fits underneath and it leaves a mark or presses on the wrist bone.
checklist.tooLoose: More than two fingers fit, and it dangles well away from the wrist.

checklist.good: It rests just above or lightly on the wrist bone and slides a little when you move your arm.
checklist.tooTight: It sits fixed above the bone and digs in when you bend your hand.
checklist.tooLoose: It slips down past the wrist bone onto your hand whenever you lower your arm.

checklist.good: It drapes evenly without twisting into a hard line or swinging loosely.
checklist.tooTight: Links stand up or twist, and the skin bulges at the edges.
checklist.tooLoose: It catches on sleeves, keyboards and bag straps.

checklist.good: The clasp tends to settle on the underside of the wrist and stays closed.
checklist.tooTight: The clasp is strained or pops open when you flex your wrist.
checklist.tooLoose: The clasp keeps swinging to the top of the wrist because the bracelet is heavy and long.

items.name: Chain bracelets
items.text: For a snug fit add about ½ in to your wrist measurement; for a comfortable drape add about ¾–1 in. Thicker chains take up more room inside, so add a little more for a heavy curb or Cuban link than for a fine chain.

items.name: Bangles
items.text: A solid bangle has to slide over the widest part of your hand, so it will always be looser on the wrist. Measure around your hand with fingers and thumb pressed together; the bangle's inside circumference should be just larger than that.

items.name: Cuff bracelets
items.text: A cuff is put on from the side through the narrow part of the wrist. It should grip lightly so it doesn't spin, with the opening on the underside of the wrist. Metal cuffs can be gently squeezed or opened, but bend them only a little and not repeatedly, or the metal can weaken or crack.

items.name: Beaded and stretch bracelets
items.text: These should roll on easily and sit with no gap but no pressure. If the beads leave a ring of dents, it's too small; if it slides over your hand, it's too big.

items.name: Men's bracelets
items.text: Men's bracelets are usually worn a little looser, often with about 1 in of room for chains and leather. Heavier links and wider wrists both call for more length. If you wear it with a watch, a looser bracelet sits more comfortably beside it.

items.name: Charm bracelets
items.text: Charms hang inward and take up room, so add about 1 in, or more if you plan to add many charms.

measure.heading: How to measure your wrist for a bracelet
steps: Wrap a soft tape measure or a strip of paper around your wrist just above the wrist bone.
Hold it snug against the skin without squeezing and note the length in inches or centimeters.
Add about ½ in for a snug fit, ¾ in for a comfortable fit, or 1 in for a loose fit. That's your bracelet length.
For a bangle, instead measure around the widest part of your hand with your thumb tucked toward your little finger.
For a cuff, measure your wrist and compare it with the cuff's inside length, adding the width of the opening.
measure.tip: If you already own a bracelet that fits well, lay it flat, open, and measure from end to end including the clasp. That's the most reliable length to shop with.

problems.problem: The bracelet slides over your hand
problems.fix: It's too long. A jeweler can remove links from most chains. For a quick fix, a bracelet with an adjustable slider or an extender used on a shorter setting helps.

problems.problem: The clasp keeps rotating to the top
problems.fix: A heavy clasp on a loose bracelet will swing to the top. Shorten the bracelet slightly, or choose a design with a counterweight or a box clasp.
Add a bracelet extender chain in matching metal, or ask a jeweler to add links.

problems.problem: A bangle won't go over your hand
problems.fix: Squeeze your fingers and thumb together, use lotion, and roll it on gently. If it still won't pass, the bangle is too small, and solid bangles generally can't be enlarged.

problems.problem: A cuff spins around the wrist
problems.fix: Squeeze it very slightly smaller with even pressure using both hands. Many cuffs adjust a little, but ask a jeweler before bending solid gold or a thick cuff.

extra.heading: Wearing a bracelet with a watch
extra.body: Wear the bracelet on the opposite wrist, or on the same wrist on the hand side of the watch, where it won't knock against the case. A slightly looser bracelet sits beside a watch more comfortably. Soft materials like leather or beads are less likely to scratch a watch than metal links.

extra.heading: Bracelets for kids
extra.body: Children's wrists change quickly, so choose adjustable slider or extender styles. Keep them loose enough to pass a finger underneath, and avoid small charms or beads for young children who might put them in their mouths.

picks.label: Bracelet extender chains
picks.why: Adds an inch or two to a bracelet that's slightly short, without permanent changes.

picks.label: Adjustable slider bracelets
picks.why: A sliding bead or toggle lets you set the exact fit, which helps if you're between sizes or buying a gift.

picks.label: Open cuff bracelets
picks.why: Cuffs go on from the side and adjust slightly, so they suit people whose hands are wide compared with their wrists.

picks.label: Men's chain bracelets by length
picks.why: Shopping by length lets you add the right amount of room for your wrist instead of relying on a single standard size.

faqs.q: Should a bracelet be tight or loose?
faqs.a: Slightly loose. You should be able to slip one or two fingers under it, and it should move a little but not slide over your hand. Very snug styles are a matter of taste, but they shouldn't press on the wrist bone.

faqs.q: How long should a bracelet be for my wrist?
faqs.a: Add about ½ in to your wrist measurement for a snug fit, ¾ in for comfortable, and 1 in for loose. A 6½ in wrist usually wears a 7–7½ in bracelet.

faqs.q: How should a chain bracelet fit?
faqs.a: A chain should drape just above the wrist bone with one to two fingers of room. Thicker chains need a little more length than fine chains to fit the same way.

faqs.q: How should a cuff bracelet fit?
faqs.a: It should sit at the narrowest part of the wrist with the opening underneath, grip lightly so it doesn't spin, and leave no marks. It shouldn't slide over your hand.

faqs.q: How should a men's bracelet fit?
faqs.a: Usually a little looser than a woman's, with about 1 in of room for chain and leather styles so it moves freely. It should still not slide over the hand.

faqs.q: How should a gold bracelet fit?
faqs.a: The same as any bracelet, but since gold is soft and valuable, avoid a fit so loose it catches and snaps, or so tight it strains the clasp.
